item.title: Fronted concession with as and though
item.explanation_text:
In formal English, you can put an adjective first to acknowledge a fact before stating a result that might seem surprising. In ‘Fragile as the model was, it survived the journey’, the opening clause means ‘Although the model was fragile’. Put as or though immediately after the adjective, then keep the usual subject–verb order and the tense the context calls for.

An adverb can go first in the same way. ‘Carefully though we packed the glass, one panel cracked’ acknowledges how we packed it. You can also front a noun that identifies someone’s role. In ‘Novice as she was, she spotted the fault’, the role noun is bare, without the article that appears in ‘Although she was a novice’.

Check the relationship between the clauses. Concessive as introduces a fact that makes the outcome unexpected. Causal as introduces a reason for the outcome, while as … as compares two things on the same scale.
item.contrast_text: ‘Unstable as the prototype was, testing continued’ means testing continued despite the instability. ‘As the prototype was unstable, testing stopped’ gives the instability as the reason for stopping. ‘The prototype was as unstable as the previous version’ compares the two versions.
item.common_error_pattern: In the bare-noun pattern, change “although he was an apprentice” to “apprentice as he was”. Keep the subject before the verb after as or though.

examples.bad: Fragile as was the model, it survived the journey.
examples.good: Fragile as the model was, it survived the journey.

examples.bad: Carefully though packed we the glass, one panel cracked.
examples.good: Carefully though we packed the glass, one panel cracked.

examples.bad: Novice as was she, she spotted the fault.
examples.good: Novice as she was, she spotted the fault.

examples.bad: Although cramped the booth was, it housed all the recording equipment.
examples.good: Cramped though the booth was, it housed all the recording equipment.

children.prompt_text: ___ the prototype was, the sensors picked up the faint click of the relay. (noisy)

children.title: A well-rehearsed account
children.instructions: Complete the opening as a concession with as. Begin with the adjective cue and follow it with as, the subject and the verb. Enter only the missing words.
children.prompt_text: ___, the guide’s account contained a striking omission. (rehearsed / it / was)

children.title: An apprentice’s observation
children.instructions: Rewrite the same sentence using just as after the role noun. Keep the subject and verb in that order and leave the main clause unchanged.
children.prompt_text: Apprentice though as he was, he noticed a hairline crack in the mounting bracket.
accepted_answers: Apprentice as he was, he noticed a hairline crack in the mounting bracket.

children.title: A portable display
children.instructions: Rewrite the same sentence, fixing only the subject–verb order in the concessive clause.
children.prompt_text: Portable though was the display, it still took two people to carry it upstairs.
accepted_answers: Portable though the display was, it still took two people to carry it upstairs.

children.title: A gap in the recording
children.instructions: Rewrite the opening as a fronted-adverb concession. Begin with “Systematically though” and keep the main clause exactly as given.
children.prompt_text: Although we indexed the recordings systematically, we failed to note a six-minute gap in the final interview.
accepted_answers: Systematically though we indexed the recordings, we failed to note a six-minute gap in the final interview.

children.title: An unexpected test result
children.instructions: Use every slash-delimited tile once. Start with Brittle and use “the casing” as the subject of the opening clause. Keep punctuation attached to its tiles.
children.prompt_text: the casing / the drop test. / Brittle / it / as / survived / was,
accepted_answers: Brittle as the casing was, it survived the drop test.

children.title: A quieter demonstration
children.instructions: Rewrite the opening concession in a formal testing report. Begin with “Quiet as” and keep the comparison and the main clause exactly as given.
children.prompt_text: Although the revised motor was quiet, it still produced as much vibration as the original.
accepted_answers: Quiet as the revised motor was, it still produced as much vibration as the original.
